fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E at the horizon (my own 2028 non-GAAP EPS extrapolation $7.00 x 38 = $266, 60%), EV/sales on 2028 revenue ($9B x 10x + $2.45B net cash = $285, 15%) and a 10-year DCF (11% WACC, 20% FCF margin, 4% terminal growth, + $2.45B net cash = $146, 25%); ~324M diluted shares that already include the ~$195-strike 0% 2030 converts, so the converts are equity and ~$2.45B of cash is net cash.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Sep-2027 value priced on next-year earnings: 2028 non-GAAP EPS $7.00 is my extrapolation, not consensus (no FY28 consensus exists; FY27 consensus $4.93 on $6.79B revenue, 28 analysts, range $2.95-$7.01, grown ~40%) x 38x forward P/E (premium for 30-40%+ growth and AI-power scarcity, down from ~59x current forward-2027 multiple). Per-share EPS is already on a diluted basis incl. converts, so no separate cash adjustment.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2028 revenue est. $9.0B (2026 guide $3.9-4.2B, FY27 consensus ~$6.8B) x 10x EV/sales = $90B EV; + ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash ($2.67B cash at 6/30/26 less ~$0.2B financing obligations; $2.475B converts treated as equity) = $92.45B; / ~324M diluted shares

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue $6.5B (2027), 9.0, 11.5, 14.0 (2030), then growth 15/12/10/8/6% to $22.7B in 2035; FCF margin 20%; WACC 11% (beta ~3, high execution risk); terminal growth 4%; PV as of Sep-2027: explicit FCF ~$16B + TV ~$29B = EV ~$45B + ~$2.45B net cash = ~$47.5B; / ~324M diluted shares

bear.story: AI data-center capex digestion or project delays slow backlog conversion. A specific trigger: Project Jupiter (2.4 GW, largest single order) slips materially if New Mexico denies or delays the fuel-cell air permit (Nov 23, 2026 deadline) or the Energy Transfer pipeline slips beyond Feb 1, 2027 without redeployment of units to other Oracle sites; I put roughly a third of the bear weight (~10%) on a Jupiter-led reset. Otherwise scandium/China supply, tariffs or the securities suit weigh. 2028 EPS resets to ~$4.50 and the multiple compresses to ~30x; ~$7.5/share of net cash gives a small floor. Stock round-trips toward and below the July-2026 post-earnings lows (~$165).

base.story: 2026 lands near $4.1B revenue / ~$2.7 EPS; FY27 guide (Feb 2027) roughly matches consensus (~$6.8B revenue, ~$4.9 EPS) on 2 GW capacity; Jupiter proceeds with some timing shift into 2028 that is offset by non-Oracle backlog (Morgan Stanley: >$8B equipment backlog, more than half non-Oracle). Strong growth largely priced in, so the multiple de-rates as earnings catch up and the stock ends near today's level.

bull.story: Beat-and-raise pattern continues (three guidance raises in 2026); Jupiter permit granted in Nov and $20-25B total backlog plus the Brookfield $25B framework convert faster; 2027 EPS tracks the ~$7 high end and 2028 approaches $10; market keeps a 45-50x multiple on a scarce onsite AI-power standard.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150 (roughly 48% under spot, under the ~$164 post-Q2 July-2026 low) BE would trade at ~30x FY27 consensus EPS of $4.93 despite ~$7.5/share of net cash, which only makes sense with real estimate cuts: Project Jupiter actually cancelled or pushed past 2028 (air permit denied at the Nov 23, 2026 deadline or the pipeline slipping well past Feb 2027 with no redeployment), a Feb-2027 FY27 guide well below ~$6.8B revenue, hyperscaler backlog deferrals, gross margin back under ~30%, a scandium supply disruption, or a broad AI-capex pullback. Moves to $170-230 are ordinary noise for a 112%-vol stock.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. Bloom Energy (solid-oxide fuel cells) has become a leading onsite power option for AI data centers: Q2-2026 revenue $1.065B (+166% y/y), non-GAAP GM 34.3%, non-GAAP EPS $0.78, FY26 guide raised a third time to $3.9-4.2B revenue and $2.55-2.85 EPS; FY27 consensus $4.93 EPS on $6.79B revenue. The supervisor showed my round-1 balance sheet was inconsistent: the 0% 2030 converts (conversion ~$194.97) are deep in the money and already in the Q2 diluted count of 323.3M, so they are equity and ~$2.45B of cash is net cash (~$7.5/share). I now use ~324M shares plus $2.45B net cash, lifting EV/sales from $269 to $285 and DCF from $140 to $146; the P/E leg ($266, my own 2028 EPS extrapolation of $7.00 x 38) is unchanged. Blended fair value rises from $235 to $239, still below the $288.7 spot. I also missed Oracle's Sep 24 force-majeure notice on Project Jupiter; I verified it runs from Oracle to developer Blue Owl, lets Oracle defer lease payments if the 2028 target slips, and that Oracle and Blue Owl reaffirmed while Bloom says the 2.4 GW contract stands (stock fell ~6% then rebounded ~8%). The pipeline slipped to Feb 1, 2027 and the fuel-cell air permit has a Nov 23, 2026 decision deadline. I agree with the supervisor that this is mainly a timing risk (MS: >$8B equipment backlog, over half non-Oracle; units can be redeployed), so I keep the bear weight at 30% but explicitly assign ~10% of it to a Jupiter-led reset, and add a small amount of near-term event risk. Distribution: ~75% forward sigma (below 112% realized as the company scales), median ~$270-275, scenario mean ~$293 (30% $145 / 45% $285 / 25% $485). Ladder nudged up ~0.5pt at low-to-middle strikes for the net-cash correction; tails unchanged because Jupiter and net cash roughly offset there. Q3 date corrected to late Oct (likely Tue Oct 27, unannounced). Research: ~13 round-1 queries plus 3 round-2 searches; no option data consulted.
